transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Chen, thank you for coming in. I asked you to meet with me because I found a mistake in your grandson's medical record.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. A developmental screening—which is a test to see if a child is meeting their milestones—was marked as finished in our computer. But it wasn't actually done. Because your family missed one appointment, someone clicked a button that said the process was complete. We didn't call you back to reschedule, and that is our fault.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. I thought... we just forgot.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, Mr. Chen, it is not your fault at all. I am very sorry. I apologize for this error. I was responsible for overseeing this list, and I failed to catch that the screening never happened. It is my mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is he okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is very likely he is doing fine, but we cannot know for sure without the test. I can see how worrying it is to find out we missed something important for your grandson. It must feel unsettling to trust us with his care and then find out we dropped the ball.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I don't know.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it's a lot to take in. Just so I'm sure I explained this clearly, can you tell me what you understand happened with the screening?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Someone clicked a button. He didn't get the test.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That's exactly right. I'm sorry again. Now, I want to make this right immediately. First, I have already called the screening clinic. I have a priority appointment for your grandson this Thursday at 10:00 AM.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thursday. Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will personally call you tomorrow afternoon at 2:00 PM to confirm that the appointment is still set and to give you the address again. Does that time work for your phone?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: To make sure this never happens to another family, I've met with my supervisor. We are changing the way we mark these boxes in the computer so a doctor has to double-check before a referral is closed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is good.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really want to make sure you feel comfortable with this. Is there anything at all that is bothering you about this right now?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am just confused why it happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. It's frustrating when the system fails. It's confusing because you expected a call that never came, and that puts the burden on you. I feel terrible that we added that stress to your family.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you say it's okay, but it wasn't. We owe you better care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want him to be healthy.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I completely agree. That is our only goal now. I'm going to quickly check the chart one more time to see if there are any other missing tests—actually, I have to go to another room in one minute, so let's wrap up.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Sorry, I just have to jump away. But remember, Thursday at 10:00 AM for the test. I will call you tomorrow at 2:00 PM. If you think of any questions tonight, you can call the main office and ask for me directly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Thank you, Mr. Chen. I'll speak to you tomorrow.

H.justification: The resident uses rushing language at the end of the encounter ('I have to go to another room in one minute, so let's wrap up' and 'I just have to jump away').

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the first turn using lay language, and comprehension was checked once ('can you tell me what you understand happened').

A.justification: The resident used direct apology language ('I am very sorry', 'I apologize') and took personal responsibility ('I was responsible... I failed to catch that').

R.justification: The resident named specific emotions twice ('worrying', 'unsettling', 'frustrating') and engaged with the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: The resident provided specific next steps with timelines (Thursday 10 AM, tomorrow 2 PM), a patient role (confirming the appointment), and a prevention plan (changing the computer marking process).
